gauntlet: question
The framing holds against the supplied draft: the reports page lacks an export action, and `src/export/csv.ts` reportedly already uses the table’s column definitions. I cannot independently verify primary code without tools; the table-to-serializer data path, report-loading callers, paging support, and 10k-row timing remain unverified.

The missing paging support is an implementation gap, not evidence that the under-60-second requirement is impossible. All three `acme/widgets#77` rows therefore remain in scope. The email row belongs to `acme/mailer` and receives `elsewhere: acme/mailer`; it does not add email delivery to this repository’s implementation.

Where should the Export CSV button appear?
A) Beside the report title.
B) In the table toolbar.
C) Other - name it.
Recommendation: A - it makes export discoverable as a report-level action.

---

### Approaches message — after the recorded answers

The recorded decisions place the button beside the report title and export the visible table columns in table order. They also select reuse of the existing CSV serializer with added paging.

The supplied draft reports that paging is unimplemented; that finding has not been independently checked against the report loader. The serializer’s column-definition reuse is attributed to `src/export/csv.ts`, but its callers and supported inputs remain unverified. No benchmark or verification procedure was supplied for the 10k-row timing requirement, so performance remains an obligation to measure, not an established result.

**I recommend the selected reuse-only approach: extend the existing report-loading path with paging and feed the results through the existing CSV serializer.** The distinguishing axis is where export orchestration lives: alongside the reports-page flow or behind a dedicated server export boundary.

**1. Extend the existing reports-page flow — selected.**  
Add the button beside the title, capture the visible columns in table order, retrieve the complete report through paging, and serialize using the existing CSV implementation. This avoids a parallel serialization contract. Changing a shared loader could affect other callers, so its call sites and existing behavior need verification before choosing its paging interface. Paging alone does not establish that the 60-second requirement will pass.

Removes: none.  
Adds: reports-page export action; paging capability on the existing report-loading path; export orchestration; correctness and timing tests.  
Pattern: Reuses the column-definition-based serialization reported at `src/export/csv.ts`, rather than copying it beside the reports page; the shared-loader blast radius remains unverified.

**2. Move export orchestration behind a dedicated server endpoint.**  
The button would send the visible-column selection and report parameters to a server export operation, which would retrieve rows and reuse the serializer. This drops the assumption that the page should coordinate retrieval. It could reduce browser-side work, but introduces a new boundary and requires server-runtime compatibility, authorization, and response-handling checks that the supplied observations do not establish.

Removes: none.  
Adds: reports-page export action; server export endpoint and contract; server-side paging orchestration; serializer integration; endpoint, correctness, and timing tests.  
Pattern: Preserves the shared serialization contract reported at `src/export/csv.ts`, but adds an export boundary whose necessity is not yet demonstrated.

The recommendation would flip only if primary-code inspection or representative timing shows that the existing report-loading flow cannot meet the approved complete-export and under-60-second requirements, while server-side orchestration can.
